answers.answer: Select 3 randomly chosen Escape Pod tokens. Place the lowest-numbered in Section A, the next number in Section B, then continue alternating A/B; all start Locked side up. Put 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, and 7 Adults in the Intruder bag (3 Adults plus one additional Adult per player).
answers.evidence: Setup, steps 7 and 10: ‘3 for 3–4 players’; lowest-numbered pod in A, next in B, then alternate; 3 Adults plus 1 per player.

answers.answer: Remove from both Corporate and Personal Objective decks every card showing a player count above the actual player count, shuffle the decks separately, then deal each player one of each face down/hidden. At the First Encounter—the first time an Intruder miniature appears—each player chooses one of their two Objectives and removes the rejected one from the game face down, unseen by anyone. Eggs are not Intruders, so they do not trigger this choice. The summary does not specify a later opportunity to choose if no First Encounter occurs.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 16; Critical gameplay moments: ‘first time an Intruder miniature (of any type) appears’; Eggs are not Intruders.

answers.answer: Discard the Action card being used and two additional Action cards to pay its printed cost of 2, for three Action cards total. Contamination cards cannot be discarded to pay an Action cost. If the card has two sections separated by OR, choose one section/effect.
answers.evidence: Actions from Action cards: discard that card and the required additional cards; choose one when sections are separated by OR.

answers.answer: They suffer 1 Light Wound at the end of their own round, after the one Action and passing. Once passed, they cannot take further normal Actions that Player Phase, though the FAQ permits Interruption after passing. On passing, they may discard any number of cards from their hand. Later players' rounds do not cause another Fire wound to this Character that turn; Fire damage for a Character is assessed only at the end of that Character's own round.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Player rounds: ending a round in Fire causes 1 Light Wound; passing bars further normal Actions and permits discarding any number of hand cards.

answers.answer: On entry, flip the unexplored Room tile face up and reveal and resolve its Exploration token. Set the Room's Item count by rotating the tile so the token's number faces the printed Item Counter (except Nest and Room Covered in Slime); resolve the token's effect and then remove the token to the box. If the Room is empty after the exploration effect, make a Noise roll, unless the Exploration effect was Silence or Danger, which replaces/suppresses that roll. Silence does nothing; with Slime on the Character, treat it as Danger. Danger suppresses the roll and moves all eligible neighboring Intruders into the Room; if none are eligible, put Noise in each connected Corridor without a marker. If a Character or Intruder is already in the destination Room, do not roll for Noise.
answers.evidence: Movement, Rooms, and Corridors; Exploration tokens; Noise roll: flip and resolve token; set Item count; remove token to box; no Noise roll if anyone is already there.

answers.answer: Careful Movement costs 2 Action cards and replaces the post-move Noise roll with placing a Noise marker in a chosen Corridor connected to the destination. FAQ clarification says it also replaces automatic Silence/Danger Exploration results. It is forbidden in Combat and if all Corridors connected to the destination already have Noise markers. Normal Movement restrictions still apply, so a Closed Door blocks the move. A miniature cannot stop in a Corridor; characters and Intruders occupy Rooms only.
answers.evidence: Basic Actions: Careful Movement costs 2, replaces Noise roll, cannot be used in Combat, and follows restrictions including Closed Doors; Movement section: no one stops in Corridors.

answers.answer: Because a Corridor cannot hold a second Noise marker, resolve an Encounter. First discard all Noise markers from every Corridor connected to the Room, including the Technical Corridors space if connected. Draw one token from the bag and place its matching Intruder miniature; keep a non-Blank drawn token set aside outside the bag until a rule returns it. Compare the token number with the triggering player's hand size: fewer cards than the number causes a Surprise Attack against that Character; equal or more does not. Action and Contamination cards both count for this comparison.
answers.evidence: Encounters: discard all connected Noise, draw/place token, compare number to hand including Action and Contamination, set token aside; Noise roll and Technical Corridors sections.

answers.answer: Danger moves every neighboring Intruder that is not in Combat with a Character into the destination Room. If no neighboring Intruders are present, or all are in Combat, place a Noise marker in every connected Corridor that lacks one (including Technical Corridors if the Room has an Entrance). Intruder movement into a Character's Room is not an Encounter; it simply puts them in Combat. If the Character has Slime, a Silence result resolves as Danger instead.
answers.evidence: Exploration tokens/Noise roll: move all eligible Intruders; otherwise mark empty connected Corridors. Encounters: an Intruder merely moving into a Room with a Character is NOT an Encounter. Slime marker rule.

answers.answer: On a Blank in an Encounter, place a Noise marker in each Corridor connected to the Room, return the Blank to the bag, and end the Encounter without placing a miniature. If the Blank was the last token in the bag, add 1 Adult token to the bag if available; otherwise add none. In bag development, drawing a Blank adds 1 Adult token if available, with no last-token condition stated, then returns the Blank to the bag.
answers.evidence: Encounters, ‘Blank token in an Encounter’; Event Phase, Intruder bag development, ‘Blank’.

answers.answer: Both Intruders stay in their starting Room and destroy the Closed Door simultaneously. A destroyed Door is represented by a lying token, permits movement, and cannot be closed again (except with the Plasma Torch Item). A Noise-triggered appearance is not blocked by a Closed Door: an Intruder appears through that Corridor regardless of the Door.
answers.evidence: Door tokens: an Intruder trying to move through a Closed Door destroys it; multiple Intruders do so simultaneously and all stay put. Destroyed Doors can never be Closed again except Plasma Torch; Noise appearance ignores Closed Door.

answers.answer: When the Intruder enters a Technical Corridors Entrance, remove its miniature from the board, discard all its Injury markers, and return its token to the Intruder bag. Leave the Noise marker on the Technical Corridors space; it is not removed. Characters cannot normally use Technical Corridors (exceptions are the Mechanic's Technical Corridors Action card and Technical Corridor Plans Item), and Door tokens can never be placed there.
answers.evidence: Technical Corridors: Intruder disappears into ducts; injuries discarded, token returned, miniature removed; Noise remains; character exceptions and Doors rule.

answers.answer: Both ordinary Shoot and Melee cost 1 Action card; Shoot also requires a Hand Weapon with Ammo and spends 1 Ammo, while Melee draws 1 Contamination card to the top of the Action discard pile. In either action, choose one Intruder in your Room. Shoot rolls the Combat die: a miss has no Melee penalty. Melee rolls the same die, but any miss gives the Character 1 Serious Wound, and a two-hit result counts as only 1 Injury in Melee (whereas Shoot's double-hit result normally deals 2 Injuries before weapon modifications).
answers.evidence: Combat: Shoot (cost 1), Weapon/ammo and target in Room; Melee (cost 1), Contamination and miss wound; 2-Injury result is one in melee.

answers.answer: After damage, 1 Injury kills a Larva (and an Egg). For a Queen, draw 2 Intruder Attack cards and add their blood values; it dies if the total is equal to or lower than its Injury markers. A Retreat arrow on either Queen check card replaces the numerical check: the Queen flees via the Corridor number on a drawn Event card. Place an Intruder Carcass in the Room for dead Intruders other than Larvae; the text does not state a Carcass for a dead Queen as an exception, so the general non-Larva rule applies.
answers.evidence: Intruder Injuries and death: Larva/Egg die at 1; Queen/Breeder compare sum of two blood values; Retreat overrides numerical result; carcass for any dead Intruder except Larvae.

answers.answer: Before moving, resolve a separate Intruder Attack for each of the two Intruders, starting with larger types (Queen, Breeder, Adult, Larva). The Escape attack targets the escaper. If they die, their Corpse remains in the Room they tried to leave. If they survive, complete the move into the neighboring Room; since it is unexplored, explore and resolve it normally, and because it is empty, roll Noise after the move (unless its Exploration effect suppresses/replaces the roll).
answers.evidence: Character Escape: one Attack per Intruder before moving, larger first; death leaves Corpse; survivor completes move and explores/rolls Noise as usual.

answers.answer: With several Characters in the Room, the target is the one whose player has the fewest Action cards in hand. On a tie, choose the Character with the First Player token, or the next player in turn order. A hit occurs if the drawn Intruder Attack card has a symbol matching the attacking Intruder; otherwise it misses. A Larva does not draw an Attack card: remove it from the Room, place it on the target's Character board, and give the target 1 Contamination card on top of their Action discard pile. If the target already has a Larva, that Larva remains, the attacking Larva disappears, and the target still gets the Contamination card without automatic death.
answers.evidence: Intruder Attack and Infest (Larva attack); Contamination cards: newly gained card goes on top of Action discard pile.

answers.answer: Dressing one Serious Wound does not prevent death from another Wound when the Character already has 3 Serious Wounds; dressed cards still count toward the limit. Without 3 Serious Wounds, a third Light Wound clears the Light Wound track and causes a Serious Wound. Heal removes a Light Wound or discards a Dressed Serious Wound as specified by the healing effect. On death, place the Character Corpse token in the Room and drop all Heavy Objects there.
answers.evidence: Character Wounds and death: third Light Wound becomes Serious; dressed Serious Wounds still count; death at three Serious plus any Wound; corpse and Heavy Objects remain in Room.

answers.answer: Canteen and Shower scan only Contamination cards in the Character's hand and remove all non-Infected cards. An Infected card places a Larva on the board; with a Larva already there, the Character dies and a Creeper appears in the Room. Canteen also heals 1 Light Wound; Shower also removes Slime. Surgery scans all Contamination cards in the deck, hand, and discard, removes Infected cards, and removes a Larva if present. Surgery then causes 1 Light Wound, automatically passes the Character, and shuffles all cards (including the whole hand and remaining Contamination cards) into the Action deck, leaving the hand empty until next turn.
answers.evidence: Player Reference: Canteen/Shower and Surgery; Contamination section: ordinary Scan of an Infected card places Larva, second Larva kills and spawns Creeper.

answers.answer: To destroy uncarried Eggs in a Room, Shoot or Melee as if attacking them; each Injury of any type destroys one Egg. A missed Egg Melee causes neither the usual Contamination card nor the usual Serious Wound. The summary marks Contamination on a successful Egg Melee as unresolved by the manual. Grenades can be thrown at a Room containing uncarried Eggs as if an Intruder were there; a Grenade destroys 2 Eggs and a Molotov destroys 1. After every attempt to destroy an Egg, roll Noise; when throwing from another Room, roll in the thrower's Room. Fire destroys 1 uncarried Egg in that Room during each Fire Damage step. When no Eggs remain on the Intruder board, the Nest is destroyed and marked with 1 Injury marker.
answers.evidence: Eggs and the Nest; FAQ Rooms, Eggs and Items: grenade/Molotov from another Room causes Noise in your own Room.

answers.answer: Use the Evacuation Section A/B Room Action (cost 2 Action cards) when a Pod in that Section is Unlocked and has a free Character space. Resolve a Noise roll first; entry fails if an Intruder appears or is present, and entry is also barred if the Evacuation Section Room has a Malfunction. Each Pod holds 2 Characters; Heavy Objects take no Character space. After entering, launch immediately or wait; entering and waiting passes the current turn. At the start of your first round in the next Player Phase, you may stay and pass, launch, or exit for free into the Section Room and take a full round. Waiting occupants count for Noise rolls from bag development. If an Intruder appears in the Evacuation Section Room while you wait, all Characters in its Pods return to that Room. A later Malfunction does not prevent already-boarded occupants from launching, waiting, or exiting.
answers.evidence: Escape Pods; Player Reference, Evacuation Section A/B.

answers.answer: Victory checks are: (1) Engines, (2) Coordinates, (3) Contamination, (4) Objectives. If 2 or 3 Engines are Damaged, the ship explodes and everything aboard, including hibernating Characters, dies; launched Pod passengers are already away. If the ship survives but is not headed to Earth, hibernating Characters die, except a Character with the Quarantine Objective survives if the destination is Mars. Each surviving Character who is hibernating or evacuated undergoes a Contamination check: scan all Contamination cards in deck, discard, and hand; if any is Infected, shuffle all cards and draw 4, dying if any of those four is a Contamination card. A Larva skips the initial Scan and triggers the same shuffle-and-draw-four test. Thus Pod passengers do need Contamination checks. The summary does not give the exact consequence of an evacuated Character arriving on a destination other than Earth beyond its statement that launched Pod occupants are treated as having arrived on Earth.
answers.evidence: Victory Check: ordered Engines, Coordinates, Contamination, Objectives; Pod occupants always treated as arrived on Earth; contamination applies to each survivor, hibernating or evacuated.
